newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD sale not seen delayed by injunction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD sale not seen delayed by injunction.

text.p: The privatization auction of Brazil's CVRD should go ahead as planned on April 29 despite a high court injunction suspending a federal land transfer to the state-owned mining company, analysts said.
"This should not disrupt the auction. It seems the issue at stake is not that important," said Felipe Zaghen, an analyst with Banco Indosuez.

The injunction granted on Tuesday by a Supreme Federal Tribunal justice suspends the government's transfer of the right of use 411,000 hectares of land in the Carajas mining region in the northern state of Para.

Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees the privatization process, has said the court ruling does not affect the mining and exploration rights of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce SA, or CVRD, and thus does not warrant a delay of the auction. The development bank is appealing the ruling.

"I believe investors are awaiting more information," said Rodrigo Marques, an analyst with Banco Bozano, Simonsen. "There either has to be a clear decision on whether the injunction is upheld or not, or the BNDES has to clarify the matter in greater detail."
Banco Indosuez's Zaghen said investors were probably confident that the government and the BNDES would succeed in having the injunction revoked.
CVRD's mining presence in the area does not depend on the company having the right of use there, the mining sources said.

However, the right of use would grant CVRD exclusivity in the region, making it easier for the company to defend its operations against incursions by landless peasants or wildcat miners, as in the past.
A second lawsuit, questioning the constitutionality of CVRD's privatization, poses a more serious threat to the auction, Marques said.
A ruling in the high court is due on Wednesday.
